mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals increased economic activity, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it indicates a strong consumer-driven economy, which boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 50,000 over the past month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals an economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 40% of triggered instances.
